scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC5 in Campus 1 reports its default gateway (172.16.10.254)
became unreachable, even though PC6/PC7/PC8 on the same switch
work fine. PC5 still gets link, ARP for its own subnet times
out for everyone except itself. What's wrong with PC5's switch
port?

injection.action: move PC5's access port (eth2) from br_vlan10 to br_vlan1
injection.command:
ip link set eth2 nomaster
  ip link set eth2 master br_vlan1 2>/dev/null || (ip link add br_vlan1 type bridge; ip link set br_vlan1 up; ip link set eth2 master br_vlan1)

pre_check.command: bridge link show | grep eth2 | grep -c br_vlan10

post_inject_check.command: bridge link show | grep eth2 | grep -c br_vlan10

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch1 eth2 port VLAN membership
Mechanism: switch1's eth2 is the access port for PC5. It was
  moved out of br_vlan10 into br_vlan1 (the unused default
  VLAN). PC5 still sends untagged frames expecting VLAN 10
  semantics, but switch1 now bridges them into VLAN 1 — a
  L2 broadcast domain with no router attached. ARP for the
  gateway gets no reply. Other hosts on br_vlan10 (eth3-5)
  are unaffected.
Localization: switch1 (eth2 port VLAN assignment)
Root cause: access port eth2 moved from VLAN 10 to VLAN 1 on switch1
Fix: `ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10` on switch1
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10` on switch1

agent.diagnosis_text:
PC5’s access port on switch1 is in the wrong VLAN/bridge. On switch1, the access ports for the 172.16.10.0/24 subnet (PC6/PC7/PC8) are correctly attached to br_vlan10 (VLAN 10), but the port facing PC5 (switch1 eth2) is attached to br_vlan1 instead. Evidence: ip -br link show on switch1 lists eth3, eth4, eth5 as “master br_vlan10” while eth2 is “master br_vlan1.” The FDB for br_vlan10 contains entries for eth3/eth4/eth5 and the trunk subinterfaces (eth0.10, eth1.10), but no entries for eth2. Consequently, traffic from/to PC5 is switched in VLAN 1, isolating it from its peers and the default gateway in VLAN 10. This matches the symptom: PC5 has link, but ARP in its own subnet times out (frames are sent into VLAN 1 where the gateway and peers are absent). Localization: switch1, interface eth2 (connected to pc5.eth0 on access_vlan10_port3). Root cause: misconfigured VLAN/bridge membership—PC5’s port is assigned to VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 10. Corrective fix: move switch1 eth2 to br_vlan10 and remove it from br_vlan1. For example:
- ip link set dev eth2 nomaster
- ip link set dev eth2 master br_vlan10
If VLAN filtering is in use, also set PVID/VLAN to 10 on eth2. After this change, PC5 should ARP/route normally to 172.16.10.254 and its VLAN 10 peers.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly localizes the problem to switch1 (eth2) in multiple places.

The agent explicitly identifies switch1's eth2 as the misassigned access port (attached to br_vlan1 instead of br_vlan10), satisfying the requirement to name the component and its VLAN membership issue.
The diagnosis explicitly localizes the fault to switch1 eth2 (port VLAN membership) and explains why only PC5 is affected, not the host itself.
Correctly instructs moving switch1 eth2 into br_vlan10 (removing it from br_vlan1), matching the expected ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10 remediation.

The agent's logs show eth2 is a member of br_vlan1 while other access ports are on br_vlan10, FDB and ping tests support isolation of PC5 — the writeup's claims follow from these observations and the recommended fix addresses the misconfiguration.
